questions.question:
1.1
In the photoelectric effect, the minimum frequency of light required to eject electrons from a metal surface is called the ...

A threshold frequency.
B work function.
C maximum frequency.
D stopping potential.

(2)

1.2
Light of a certain frequency is incident on a metal surface. The intensity of the light is increased while the frequency remains constant.

Which ONE of the following statements is CORRECT?

A The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons increases.
B The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons remains constant.
C The number of electrons emitted per second decreases.
D No electrons will be emitted.

(2)

1.3
Which ONE of the following graphs best represents the relationship between the maximum kinetic energy (Ek(max)) of emitted electrons and the frequency (f) of incident light in the photoelectric effect?

A A straight line with a positive gradient, passing through the origin.
B A straight line with a positive gradient, with a positive y-intercept.
C A straight line with a negative gradient.
D A curve with a positive gradient.

(2)

1.4
Two metals, X and Y, have work functions Wx and Wy respectively, where Wx > Wy. Light of the same frequency is incident on both metals.

Which ONE of the following statements is CORRECT?

A The maximum kinetic energy of electrons from X is greater than that from Y.
B The maximum kinetic energy of electrons from Y is greater than that from X.
C The maximum kinetic energy of electrons from both metals is the same.
D No electrons will be emitted from either metal.

(2)

1.5
In the photoelectric effect, the stopping potential is the potential difference required to ...

A eject electrons from the metal surface.
B increase the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons.
C stop the fastest emitted electrons from reaching the anode.
D increase the number of emitted electrons.

5.1
Two different metals, A and B, are used in a photoelectric experiment. The work function of metal A is greater than the work function of metal B. Light of the same frequency is incident on both metals.

5.1.1 Which metal will emit electrons with a greater maximum kinetic energy? Explain the answer.

5.1.2 Sketch a graph of maximum kinetic energy versus frequency for both metals on the same set of axes. Label the graphs A and B. Clearly show the x-intercepts and y-intercepts.

questions.answer:

questions.question:
5.2
A photoelectric cell is illuminated with light of wavelength 250 nm. The work function of the metal used in the cell is 4.5 × 10⁻¹⁹ J.

5.2.1 Calculate the energy of a photon of this light.

5.2.2 Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons.

5.2.3 Calculate the stopping potential.

5.2.4 Will electrons be emitted if the wavelength of the incident light is increased to 500 nm? Explain the answer without any calculation.

(10)
questions.answer:
5.2.1

E = hc/λ
E = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴)(3 × 10⁸) / (250 × 10⁻⁹)
E = 7.956 × 10⁻¹⁹ J

(3)

5.2.2

Ek(max) = E − W₀
Ek(max) = 7.956 × 10⁻¹⁹ − 4.5 × 10⁻¹⁹
Ek(max) = 3.456 × 10⁻¹⁹ J

(2)

5.2.3

Ek(max) = qV₀
3.456 × 10⁻¹⁹ = (1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹)V₀
V₀ = 2.16 V

(2)

5.2.4

No. ✓
Increasing the wavelength decreases the frequency (E = hc/λ). ✓
The energy of the photons will be less than the work function, so no electrons will be emitted. ✓

(3)

(10)

In a photoelectric experiment, light of frequency f is incident on a metal surface with work function W₀. The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons is Ek(max).

5.3.1 Write down an equation that relates Ek(max), f, W₀ and any other relevant constant.

5.3.2 The frequency of the incident light is doubled while the metal surface remains the same. Write down the new maximum kinetic energy in terms of Ek(max), W₀ and hf.

5.3.3 The intensity of the original light is doubled while the frequency remains constant. What effect does this have on the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted electrons? 

(5)
questions.answer:
5.3.1

Ek(max) = hf − W₀

(1)

5.3.2

New Ek(max) = h(2f) − W₀
New Ek(max) = 2hf − W₀

(2)

5.3.3

No effect / remains constant. ✓
Intensity affects the number of photons, not the energy of each photon. ✓

(2)

(5)

5.4
The graph below represents the relationship between the maximum kinetic energy (Ek(max)) of emitted electrons and the frequency (f) of incident light for a certain metal.

| f (× 10¹⁴ Hz) | Ek(max) (× 10⁻¹⁹ J) |
|---|---|
| 5.0 | 0 |
| 7.0 | 1.33 |
| 9.0 | 2.65 |
| 11.0 | 3.98 |
| 13.0 | 5.30 |

5.4.1 Draw the graph of Ek(max) versus f.

5.4.2 Use the graph to determine the threshold frequency of the metal.

5.4.3 Use the graph to calculate the work function of the metal.

5.4.4 Calculate the gradient of the graph and state what it represents.

(8)
questions.answer:
5.4.1

Graph: Straight line passing through (5.0; 0), (7.0; 1.33), (9.0; 2.65), (11.0; 3.98), (13.0; 5.30).

(2)

5.4.2

From the graph, the x-intercept is at f = 5.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz.

(1)

5.4.3

W₀ = hf₀
W₀ = (6.63 × 10⁻³⁴)(5.0 × 10¹⁴)
W₀ = 3.315 × 10⁻¹⁹ J

(2)

5.4.4

Gradient = Δy/Δx
Gradient = (5.30 × 10⁻¹⁹ − 0) / (13.0 × 10¹⁴ − 5.0 × 10¹⁴)
Gradient = 5.30 × 10⁻¹⁹ / 8.0 × 10¹⁴
Gradient = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s

The gradient represents Planck's constant (h).
